display.purpose: The cemetery name and each specimen heading. One per sheet. Archivo Narrow 700, uppercase, line-height 1.02, tracking -0.005em.

headline.purpose: The born-died line under a heading. Source Serif 4 with tabular numerals, Ink Soft.

title.purpose: A value printed on the label. The most-read size in the system; never set in caps.

body.purpose: Determination statement, how-to-read notes, colophon. Capped near 62ch.

label.purpose: Field names, drawer headings, kickers. Archivo Narrow 600, uppercase, 0.14em tracking, Ink Faint.

mark.purpose: The smallest band, 0.58 to 0.68rem: seam marks, last-seen flag, captions, chip and toggle text.

stamp.purpose: Courier Prime identifiers: accession numbers, provenance values, the raw record.

shadows.name: sheet-contact
shadows.purpose: The only structural elevation in the system. Reserved for the specimen sheet: hard contact line, tight drop, warm inset vignette at the paper's edges.

shadows.name: slip-offset
shadows.purpose: Flat unblurred offset in the contested hue, reading as a pasted slip. Correction slip only.

motion.name: mc-pin
motion.value: 220ms ease-out both; opacity 0 to 1 with translateY(4px) to 0
motion.purpose: The sheet, provenance panel, and variant splay animate in as if put down. Gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: seam-grow
motion.purpose: The rust version-seam is a repeating 6px by 2px gradient so that it can grow on a claim value.

material.name: generated-paper
material.value: Two inline SVG feTurbulence layers on the sheet: fine fibre (baseFrequency .9, 4 octaves, 140px tile, opacity .05) and slow mottle (baseFrequency .006, 3 octaves, seed 7, 620px tile, opacity .055), both desaturated via feColorMatrix saturate 0.
material.purpose: The sheet's material. Never replaced by a flat fill or a bitmap asset.

material.name: mounting-grid
material.value: body background: two 1px linear-gradients at 2rem intervals, rgba(120, 134, 118, .10)
material.purpose: The faint grid of a mounting sheet on the board, deliberately below the threshold of pattern.

material.name: mounting-corners
material.value: sheet ::before and ::after, 1.6rem squares, 2px solid #cbd2c6, inset 0.45rem, pointer-events none
material.purpose: Four corners hold the specimen down. Two corners is not the motif; four is.

conventions.name: most-asserted
conventions.value: pick(): sort contested claims by assertion count descending, then createdAt descending; blank values excluded unless all are blank.
conventions.purpose: A contested line leads with the value asserted most often, newest wins a tie. Stated convention, not a verdict; the page says so.

conventions.name: stray-slip
conventions.value: template.stray(): keys outside FIELDS render in the stray variant below the determination, never as catalog claim rows.
conventions.purpose: Reproduces records the exhibit did not make while keeping them off the label proper.

conventions.name: linked-only
conventions.value: LINKED_ONLY = ["depiction"]: depictions render as an empty mounting space plus an attributed outbound link, never as an image element.
conventions.purpose: The exhibit does not hold the rights and will not mount a meme on a dead child's sheet.

conventions.name: deep-link
conventions.value: #specimen/<encodeURIComponent(normalized IRI)>; localStorage key mc:lastSeen drives the last-seen mark.
conventions.purpose: A specimen sheet is citable: the address is the record.

conventions.name: accession
conventions.value: shortId(): last path segment of the normalized IRI, truncated to 12 characters with an ellipsis. Drawer rows number 0001 onward by position.
conventions.purpose: Identifiers are typed stamps, not set type.

narrative.overview: The exhibit is a herbarium and museum mounting sheet, not a profile page. A specimen is fixed to a cool grey-green board by four corners, carries a printed label with an accession number and a determination line, and is filed in a drawer with an index. That institutional form was chosen because it is the artifact that already knows how to handle this project's exact situation: a hand-made catalog whose compiler is unrecorded, transcribed page by page into a linked-data store. An institutional sheet does not claim to be the thing it describes. It claims to be a record about it, made by someone, at a date, and it prints that trail. So every value on the page is rendered as a claim with an accession behind it, and a claim is either supported or marked. The aesthetic consequence is restraint with one exception: the sheet is allowed to be physically present. Generated paper fibre, a faint mounting grid on the board, four mounting corners, and a pasted slip that casts a small offset shadow are the entire amount of materiality permitted. Everything else is typography and rules. Colour is never used to decorate, warm, or enliven; there are exactly two accents and each of them is a statement about evidence, so an accent applied for any other reason is a defect, not a style choice. The palette is deliberately cool: a grey-green board and off-white sheet under a single near-black ink. It is emphatically not cream, not sepia, and not parchment. The reading order is also a design constraint. The primary audience is students, possibly as young as secondary school, arriving cold with no context. The sheet must be legible before it is navigable.
keyCharacteristics: A cool grey-green mounting board, an off-white sheet, one ink; no cream, no sepia.
Two accents with fixed meanings: green is evidence, rust is disagreement. Neither decorates.
Three faces with fixed jobs: condensed institutional caps for labels, a reading serif for values, monospace for identifiers.
Surfaces are square-edged and held by hairline rules, never by radius or by accent tabs.
Absence is a drawn state: an empty dashed mounting space, never a placeholder or a stock image.
Every claim line is a press target that opens the record asserting it.

rules.name: The Two Accents Rule
rules.body: Green means evidence. Rust means disagreement. Neither is decorative, neither is a brand colour, and neither may be used for emphasis, hierarchy, decoration, or because this needs colour. For every green or rust element on a screen, name what it asserts; if you cannot name it, remove it.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: People who are dead are printed in ink. No accent, tint, wash, or highlight is ever applied to a name, a date of birth, or a date of death.

rules.name: The Cool Board Rule
rules.body: The paper is cool. Off-white sheet on grey-green board. Cream, parchment, beige, sepia, and warm greys are excluded.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Archivo Narrow labels, Source Serif 4 states values, Courier Prime identifies. A type role never crosses.

rules.name: The Student Floor Rule
rules.body: Values stay in the reading serif at 1.06rem or larger and body prose at 17px/1.55. Uppercase and letterspacing are reserved for labels and marks. Density never wins an argument with a fifteen-year-old arriving by accident.

rules.name: The Orientation Before Navigation Rule
rules.body: On every viewport, including the narrowest where the drawer jumps the queue, the visitor reads what the exhibit is before being asked to choose anything.

rules.name: The Paper-Only Depth Rule
rules.body: Only the sheet casts a real shadow, and only a pasted slip casts an offset one. A new panel communicates state with the sheet-edge tone and a 1px rule.

rules.name: The Generated Paper Rule
rules.body: The sheet's texture is two inline SVG feTurbulence layers. Do not replace them with a flat fill or a downloaded paper JPG.

rules.name: The Press-Any-Line Rule
rules.body: Every claim row is a button that opens the record asserting it. A value that cannot be traced must not be printed as a claim row.

rules.name: The Most-Asserted Rule
rules.body: A contested line leads with the value the records assert most often; a tie goes to the more recent claim. It is a stated convention, not a verdict, and the page says so out loud. Never silently re-order contested values by recency, and never resolve a disagreement by dropping a variant.

rules.name: The Slip Rule
rules.body: Keys outside the catalog's vocabulary are reproduced but go on a labelled slip below the determination, never as a claim row on the label proper.

rules.name: The Linked-Not-Mounted Rule
rules.body: Depictions are never rendered as an image element. The exhibit shows an empty mounting space and an attributed outbound link. No future work may mount third-party imagery, fabricate imagery, or fill an empty mount with a stand-in.

dos: Do keep the two accents' meanings intact: evidence green for anything backed by a record, contested rust for anything the records disagree about.
Do build on the existing surfaces - board ground, sheet paper, sheet-edge for hover/expanded/inset - and stay inside the pad and gutter tokens for gutters.
Do set labels in Archivo Narrow uppercase with 0.1-0.16em tracking, values in Source Serif 4, identifiers in Courier Prime.

Do express edges with rules: 1px rule or rule-fine for structure, a 2px or 3px green top rule for authority, a full 1px rust border plus offset shadow for a correction slip, a dashed rule for absence.
Do mark a selected item with an inset 1px green box-shadow on the evidence wash.
Do draw empty states as the mounting space with final copy. No placeholder text ships.
Do keep the sheet's generated feTurbulence paper, its four mounting corners, and the body's 2rem mounting grid.
Do preserve the deep-link and memory contract: #specimen/<encoded IRI> and the mc:lastSeen key.
Do keep contrast at WCAG 2.1 AA and the layout usable at 375px, and keep every motion effect inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
Do let the institution bar, the raw-record viewer, and the flash bands invert to ink-on-white; those are the world's own reversed materials.
donts: Don't use a thick coloured border-left accent tab on a card, panel, or list item; this build removed that pattern deliberately. A 1px neutral rule left edge on an indented claim row is not this pattern.
Don't use cream, parchment, beige, sepia, or any warm paper. The board is cool grey-green.
Don't use green or rust as decoration, hierarchy, or emphasis, and don't tint a name or a burial date with any accent.
Don't render a depiction as an image element, link to an image file you do not hold rights to, or fill an empty mount with stock, generated, or folksy local-history photography.
Don't round corners. The single 1px radius on the seam mark is the whole exception.
Don't add blurred elevation to claim rows, chips, or trace panels.
Don't order a contested line by newest claim, and don't hide a variant to make a sheet look tidy.
Don't promote a stray key into the catalog's claim list, and don't delete one either.
Don't add a hero image, a search field, or any chrome above the sheet in the first viewport.
Don't gamify, animate for delight, or apply a playful flourish to a burial record. The tone bar is respect.
Don't ship placeholder text, and don't invent plot or parcel information - parcel outlines come from modern assessor records and the copy must keep saying so.
